entries.note: Terrain shading.

entries.note: Rivers, lakes and coastline.

entries.name: USGS — protected areas by manager (PAD-US 4.1)
entries.note: Who manages each protected area, from the current edition of the database — Forest Service, Bureau of Land Management, National Park Service, state, local, tribal or private. Drawn fresh for each view, so it takes a moment longer to appear.

entries.name: USGS — contours
entries.note: Topographic contour lines for the United States at multiple scales.

entries.name: USGS — NHD hydrography (detailed)
entries.note: Individual stream reaches, named water bodies, canals, drainage basins and other features from the National Hydrography Dataset. More detail than the cached hydrography basemap.

entries.name: NLCD — land cover
entries.note: What the land is covered with across the contiguous US and Alaska: forest, shrub, grassland, wetland, cultivated and urban, at 30 m resolution. Multiple editions of the National Land Cover Database.

entries.name: USFWS — National Wetlands Inventory
entries.note: Wetlands mapped by the US Fish & Wildlife Service: marshes, swamps, bogs, ponds and coastal waters. Useful for assessing trafficability in soft or seasonally flooded terrain.

entries.name: EPA — ecoregions
entries.note: Level III and IV ecoregions — areas where ecosystems, vegetation, soils and land use are broadly similar. Useful as context when interpreting terrain and vegetation layers.

entries.name: NOAA — snow analysis
entries.note: Daily snow water equivalent and snow depth from the NOAA National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center. Useful for planning winter access.

entries.name: USFS — fire history
entries.note: Wildfire occurrence points and perimeters in US National Forests since the 1970s. Useful for understanding which areas have burned and assessing post-fire terrain.

entries.name: USFS — fire, current edition
entries.note: The most recently published compilation of wildfire occurrences in National Forests. More current than the historical archive but otherwise covers the same data.

entries.name: USFS — fire severity (MTBS)
entries.note: How intensely each large wildfire burned, derived from satellite imagery, since 1984. From the Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity program. Useful for assessing vegetation recovery and post-fire trafficability.

entries.name: USFS — fireshed registry
entries.note: Firesheds and their treatment priority across the contiguous US — areas where prescribed burning and fuel reduction are planned or in progress.

entries.name: USGovunits
entries.note: Outlines and names of national forests, wilderness areas, parks, monuments, Bureau of Land Management and tribal lands, and state, county and town limits. Names are separate layers: pick a boundary and its label together.

entries.name: US Census — boundaries (TIGERweb)
entries.note: State, county, city and tribal-land boundaries with their names, from the Census Bureau, alongside the statistical areas it draws for its own counts.

entries.name: USGS — 3DEP elevation
entries.note: Elevation, slope and hillshade.

entries.note: Weather, radar and marine observations.
